title: Reconstruct the Certificate Issuance Lifecycle
prompt: Put the steps for obtaining and validating a server certificate in order, from key generation to revocation in case of compromise.

items.label: Generate the key pair locally and retain the private key
Create the CSR with the public key and identity (CN, SAN)
Submit the CSR to the Certificate Authority
The CA validates the requester's identity per its policy
The CA signs the certificate with its private key
Deploy the certificate and intermediate chain on the server
The client validates the chain, validity period, and hostname
In case of compromise, request revocation (CRL/OCSP)

explain: The private key never leaves the requester: the CSR only carries the public key and proof of possession. The CA validates and then signs. The client walks the chain up to a trusted root and checks revocation. Revocation occurs after issuance, in case of compromise or departure.
